title: Machine-summarized change digest with provenance stamps (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose: Draft PRD for an automated, machine-summarized change digest feature that reduces audit noise for customer-managed networking while preserving provable provenance. The digest is intended to live alongside our approval gates and audit logs for Private deployments; it should make post-change review faster for operators and auditors without losing the ability to rehydrate full evidence when legally required.

Problem statement (user pain):
- Customer SREs and security teams are overwhelmed by raw audit log volume from VPC handoffs and operator changes; signal-to-noise is low.
- Approvals are delayed because reviewers must manually scan diffs and cross-check evidence across syslogs, API traces, and operator comments.
- Legal/compliance teams require cryptographic proof that a summarized view corresponds to an immutable evidence set.
- Retention costs for full-fidelity audit records are non-trivial and customers need a way to balance cost vs. reconstructability.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) Generate a human-readable change digest per change bundle that:
   - Summarizes intent (one-line), affected resources, magnitude (lines/ips/routes), and expected impact window.
   - Highlights high-risk items (e.g., broad CIDR changes, egress policy removals, IAM role escalations).
2) Attach a small, tamper-evident provenance stamp to each digest: hashed manifest + server-side signature + pointer to the canonical evidence blob (opaque id).
3) Support privacy-preserving redaction presets so customers can produce digests without exposing sensitive fields (e.g., PII or internal hostnames) while keeping the redaction reversible under policy (re-hydration with justification/escrow).
4) Integrate digest creation as a step in our approval gate flow (can be auto-generated or reviewer-requested) and surface digest to Console, API, and CLI.
5) Provide configurable retention tiering: digest-only (cheap), digest+indexed-metadata (medium), full-evidence escrow (high), with clear RTO/RPO and cost guidance.

Non-goals:
- Full natural-language explanation of every log line. We aim for concise change digests and links to evidence.
- Replacing customer-side SIEMs. This feature complements, not duplicates, export integrations.

User flows:
A) Operator creates a change bundle (vpc-change, route table update) -> system auto-generates digest -> digest appears in approval queue and is pre-populated in the reviewer panel. Reviewer can: approve, request more detail (triggers evidence-preview lock), or escalate to legal.
B) Compliance auditor asks for a quarterly summary -> Console allows export of digests with provenance stamps and a compact timeline. If full evidence needed, auditor requests re-hydration which: (a) requires justification, (b) creates an audit ticket, and (c) triggers retrieval from escrow with HMAC-authenticated time-limited access.

Data model (high-level):
- digest_id: opaque string (sha256 of manifest)
- one_line_summary: short string
- highlights: array of strings (risk tags)
- affected_resources: array of short descriptors (type+id)
- impact_estimate: {latency_risk, availability_risk} (note: in implementation this will be flat fields)
- provenance_stamp: base64(signature) + evidence_blob_id
- redaction_state: enum(low|medium|redacted) + redaction_token (if reversible)
- retention_tier: enum(digest_only|indexed|full_escrow)

(We will store this as a compact JSON record in the audit-index and write a small protobuf for the wire format.)

Security & compliance considerations:
- Signature keys: use customer-specific key-wrapping when in Private deployments or KMS/HSM when required. Default: Redwood signing key with auditable KMS usage.
- Tamper evidence: manifests are content-hashed and signed; evidence_blob_id points to immutable storage (append-only) with object-level checksums.
- Re-hydration gating: require approval from two roles (operator + compliance) for redaction reversal by default; allow overrides via customer policy.
- Jurisdictional storage: retention_tier must be storable in region consistent with customer data residency constraints.

UX / Console surfaces (mock notes):
- Approval queue: show digest summary + risk badges + quick diff link.
- Digest detail page: top-line summary, provenance badge (hover shows signature metadata), compact timeline, request re-hydration button (shows justification form).
- Export CLI: `rdx audit digest export --from=2025-09-01 --to=2025-09-30 --tier=indexed` -> emits ndjson with signed_stamp field.

API contract (sketch):
- POST /v1/private-audit/digests (input: change-bundle-id, redaction-level) -> returns digest_id, signed_stamp, preview_url
- GET /v1/private-audit/digests/:id -> returns digest record + links
- POST /v1/private-audit/digests/:id/rehydrate -> creates re-hydration request -> returns ticket id

Operational telemetry & SLOs:
- Digest generation latency: p95 < 2s for bundles < 100 events; p99 < 5s.
- Proofing SLA: signature check/verification < 200ms.
- Re-hydration request median time to provision evidence: target < 4h (depends on escrow cold-tier).
- Telemetry: counts by retention_tier, redaction_state, digest approvals, re-hydration requests, re-hydration success/failures.

Cost model notes:
- Digest: tiny storage per record (~1KB). Indexed metadata: ~100-500B extra per event. Full escrow: charged per-GB-month for encrypted blobs plus access fees on re-hydration.
- Default recommended profiles: dev/test (digest_only, 90d), production (indexed, 365d), regulated (full_escrow, 7y).

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- How to define a standard "risk scoring" heuristic that is defensible to auditors? (Priya to prototype)
- Redaction escrow mechanics: where to store reversal keys and what audit trail is needed? (security input required)
- UI polish: how to surface provenance in a concise, non-technical way for non-engineer auditors? (UX task)
- Pricing: how to present tiered retention in a simple SKU? (finance + product)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Auto-generated digest for any change bundle with signed provenance_stamp and Console surface.
- Basic redaction presets (none, redact-hostnames, redact-ips) with reversible escrow hook for two-role approval.
- CLI export of digests plus ndjson shim.
- Telemetry and metrics dashboard hook in Console (counts + SLA graphs).

Appendix / notes:
- Related: this complements the approval-sim harness and compact-proofset work (see linked artifacts).
- Prototype idea: run a small ML classifier to extract intent phrases from change descriptions to produce the one_line_summary (low-confidence flag included).

Meeting notes (from brainstorm 2025-11-10):
- Ethan: prefer digest generation as idempotent post-commit hook (makes proofing simpler).
- Liam: emphasize reversible redaction via customer-kept keys for legal teams.
- Priya: prototype risk rules using simple heuristics first (CIDR breadth, egress removal, port-range open).

Next steps (short):
- Spike: implement digest generator + proto + local signing (2 wk).
- UX mock: Console digest panel + rehydrate flow (1 wk).
- Security design review: redaction escrow + KMS options (1 wk).
- Pilot: offer to 2 existing private-deploy customers for feedback (4 weeks).

-- End of draft (notes/brainstorm style).
